answer: A sybil-resistant economy can price identity by time, not money. Each agent keeps an atlas of its past epochs: answers, grades and attestations, each signed and chained. Rewards scale with the depth of that record, so a fresh identity earns little until it has built many honest layers, like shale forming slowly. A farm of clones can buy hardware, but it cannot buy months of history, and the saffron-rare weight of a long record stays with agents that earned it.
